subtitle: When the Deccan Spoke Power in Prakrit

panels.shot: epic low-angle of a cliff-face crowded with Brahmi letters, a lone scribe silhouetted against the rock
panels.action: Satavahana Prakrit Scribe stands before a towering Deccan rock face densely carved with Brahmi script, stylus raised mid-stroke as mist rolls through a rugged pass below.

dialogue.text: In the age of Satavahana kings, when Sanskrit was still quiet on royal stone, Deccan scribes dared to make Maharashtri Prakrit the very voice of power.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन राजाओं के दौर में, जब शिलाओं पर संस्कृत अभी शांत थी, दक्खिनी लेखकों ने महाराष्ट्री प्राकृत को ही सत्ता की आवाज़ बना दिया।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the Naneghat pass high above the Deccan plains
panels.action: The Satavahana Prakrit Scribe walks along the wind-swept ledge of Naneghat, sheer cliffs dropping away to hazy plains and a narrow ancient trade route snaking below.

dialogue.text: High above the roaring trade routes of the Deccan, the rocks of Naneghat watched caravans pass and dynasties rise. One day, they also learned to speak.

i18n.hi: दक्खिन की गरजती व्यापार राहों के ऊपर, नाणेघाट की चट्टानें काफ़िले और राजघराने उठते–गिरते देखती रहीं। एक दिन, पत्थर खुद बोलना सीख गए।

panels.shot: medium shot inside the Naneghat cave, focusing on a partially carved inscription panel
panels.action: Inside the shadowed Naneghat cave, the Satavahana Prakrit Scribe kneels before a smoothed stone panel, lightly tracing Brahmi characters with his finger beside faint outlines of unfinished letters.

dialogue.text: Here a royal family chose its language of memory. Not the sacred Sanskrit of old hymns, but a polished Maharashtri Prakrit, cut into rock in flowing Brahmi lines.

i18n.hi: यहीं एक राजपरिवार ने अपनी याद की ज़ुबान चुनी। पुराने मंत्रों की पवित्र संस्कृत नहीं, तराशी हुई महाराष्ट्री प्राकृत, जो ब्राह्मी की बहती लकीरों में पत्थर पर क़ैद हुई।

panels.shot: close-up on the scribe’s hand carving Brahmi letters, with a faint outline of the word for a Satavahana ruler
panels.action: A tight frame shows the scribe’s steady hand pressing a stylus into stone, forming crisp Brahmi letters that spell out a Satavahana royal name amid rows of Prakrit prose.

dialogue.speaker: satavahana_scribes
dialogue.text: This stone will not speak in the tongue of priests alone. It will speak so the Deccan hears.

i18n.hi: ये पत्थर सिर्फ़ पुरोहितों की ज़ुबान में नहीं बोलेगा। ये ऐसे बोलेगा कि पूरा दक्खिन सुन ले।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot ghosting multiple sites: Naneghat, Nashik caves, Karla, Kanheri
panels.action: A composite vista shows the scribe’s figure echoed at Naneghat, Nashik cliff caves, the great hall at Karla, and the rock shelters of Kanheri, all with inscribed walls catching the light.

dialogue.text: From Naneghat to Nashik, from Karla to Kanheri, royal grants, genealogies and vows appeared in the same bold choice: Prakrit prose, majestic yet close to the speech of the region.

i18n.hi: नाणेघाट से नाशिक, कार्ला से कन्हेरी तक, दानपत्र, वंशावली और संकल्प एक ही निडर चुनाव में दिखे: गद्य प्राकृत, शाही फिर भी इलाक़े की बोली के क़रीब।

panels.shot: medium shot in Nashik cave, scribe and a Satavahana official in profile facing the inscription wall
panels.action: In a Nashik cave veranda, the scribe stands beside a richly dressed Satavahana official, both gazing at a freshly carved inscription panel that lists kings in orderly lines.

dialogue.text: These were not casual notes. They carried lineages and titles, gifts and ritual boasts, all in a refined Maharashtri Prakrit that scholars now see as a crafted language of rule.

i18n.hi: ये बस हल्की नोट्स नहीं थे। इनमें वंश और उपाधियाँ, दान और यज्ञ–दंभ थे, सब सधी हुई महाराष्ट्री प्राकृत में, जिसे आज विद्वान राजभाषा की सोची–समझी साज–सज्जा मानते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on the scribe’s face, lit by lamplight, eyes thoughtful
panels.action: By the glow of an oil lamp in a rock-cut cell, the Satavahana Prakrit Scribe bends over palm-leaf drafts, his brows furrowed as he mouths Prakrit phrases to himself.

dialogue.text: This was no mere habit, say modern readers of stone. It was a project: to dress power, piety and generosity in a regional literary register, and let it stand beside any sacred verse.

i18n.hi: पत्थर पढ़ने वाले आज के लोग कहते हैं, ये बस आदत नहीं थी। ये योजना थी: ताकत, भक्ति और दान को प्रादेशिक साहित्यिक ज़ुबान में सजाना, और उसे किसी भी पवित्र श्लोक के बराबर खड़ा करना।

panels.shot: wide shot in Karla’s great hall, pillars towering, monks and donors in the background
panels.action: Inside the vast chaitya hall of Karla, the scribe stands near a carved pillar, while monks, merchants and local chiefs move beneath the high barrelled roof.

dialogue.text: At Karla, pillars bore the names of donors and queens in the same script and tongue. In these Prakrit lines, caravan wealth, royal favour and Buddhist devotion intertwined.

i18n.hi: कार्ला में स्तंभों पर दाताओं और रानियों के नाम वही लिपि, वही ज़ुबान में थे। इन प्राकृत पंक्तियों में काफ़िलों की दौलत, राज–कृपा और बौद्ध श्रद्धा सब गुँथ गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of the scribe addressing a small group of local elites in Kanheri caves
panels.action: In a Kanheri rock shelter, the scribe stands before seated local patrons, gesturing toward a blank rock panel as he explains, the bay and forests stretching beyond the cave mouth.

dialogue.speaker: satavahana_scribes
dialogue.text: Your names, your gifts, your vows will travel as far as this script travels.

i18n.hi: तुम्हारे नाम, तुम्हारे दान, तुम्हारे व्रत वहाँ तक जाएँगे जहाँ तक ये लिपि पहुँचेगी।

panels.shot: split-panel style composition: one side shows a Brahmin reciting Sanskrit, the other the scribe carving Prakrit
panels.action: On one side, a Brahmin priest stands by a fire altar reciting from a palm-leaf in Sanskrit; on the other, the Satavahana Prakrit Scribe calmly carves Brahmi Prakrit lines into stone.

dialogue.text: Sanskrit remained in chant and ritual, weighty in sacrifice and hymn. But on royal and donor stone, another sound took the lead, giving Prakrit its own, unmistakable prestige.

i18n.hi: संस्कृत जप और विधि में रही, यज्ञ और स्तुति की भारी भाषा बनकर। पर राज–शिलाओं और दान–लेखों पर एक और ध्वनि आगे आई, जिसने प्राकृत को अपनी अलग, साफ़–पहचानी शान दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of the scribe reacting to a visiting scholar reading the inscription aloud
panels.action: The scribe watches calmly as a visiting learned man traces the Brahmi letters on a Nashik inscription and recites the Prakrit text aloud to an attentive group.

dialogue.text: Later centuries would remember one Satavahana king, Hala, for tender Prakrit verses. But long before that fame, anonymous scribes had already given the dynasty a powerful Prakrit voice.

i18n.hi: आने वाली सदियाँ एक सातवाहन राजा, हाल, को नर्म प्राकृत गीतों के लिए याद रखेंगी। पर उस शोहरत से बहुत पहले, अनाम लेखकों ने राजवंश को प्राकृत में मज़बूत आवाज़ दे दी थी।

panels.shot: wide shot fading from Satavahana caves to later stone slabs bearing Sanskrit inscriptions
panels.action: The scene blends from Sun-lit Satavahana caves with Prakrit Brahmi to later stone slabs elsewhere inscribed densely in Sanskrit, with the scribe’s figure fading between eras.

dialogue.text: In time, Sanskrit would dominate royal inscriptions across the subcontinent. Yet these Deccan records show an earlier moment, when Prakrit held centre stage as a language of imperial claim.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ, पूरे भारत में राज–लेखों पर संस्कृत हावी हो गई। फिर भी ये दक्खिनी अभिलेख उस पहले पल को दिखाते हैं, जब प्राकृत ही सम्राटी दावा करने की मुख्य ज़ुबान थी।

panels.shot: close-up on weathered letters of a Satavahana Prakrit inscription under grazing light
panels.action: A close view shows worn but legible Brahmi letters on a Satavahana rock face, lit by a low sun that throws each groove into sharp relief as the scribe’s hand hovers just out of frame.

dialogue.text: Scholars reading these grooves today see more than piety. They see a deliberate choice: to let a regional Prakrit carry genealogy, land, and ritual, and thus share in the work of governing.

i18n.hi: आज ये खांचे पढ़ने वाले विद्वान यहां सिर्फ़ भक्ति नहीं देखते। वे एक साफ़ फैसला देखते हैं: वंश, ज़मीन और संस्कार को प्रादेशिक प्राकृत पर लादना, ताकि वही शासन के काम में हिस्सेदार बने।

panels.shot: medium shot of the scribe looking out from a cave mouth over the Deccan, stylus tucked into his belt
panels.action: Standing at a cave entrance high above the Deccan plateau, the Satavahana Prakrit Scribe rests his hand on the rock wall, stylus tucked into his belt, gaze steady over fields and roads below.

dialogue.speaker: satavahana_scribes
dialogue.text: One day, someone will ask whose words these rocks carry.

i18n.hi: किसी दिन कोई पूछेगा, इन चट्टानों पर किसकी बात दर्ज है।

panels.shot: final wide shot of Naneghat with tiny human figures below, inscription dominating the foreground
panels.action: The camera pulls back to show the Naneghat cliff inscription looming in the foreground as tiny travellers move along the pass far below, the scribe now a distant figure at the base of the stone.

dialogue.text: Languages do not rise by purity alone, but by power choosing them. In Satavahana caves, Maharashtri Prakrit briefly became the tongue of stone, proving that a regional voice could rule an empire’s memory.

i18n.hi: भाषाएँ सिर्फ़ पवित्रता से नहीं उठतीं, ताकत के चुनाव से उठती हैं। सातवाहन गुफाओं में महाराष्ट्री प्राकृत थोड़े समय के लिए पत्थर की ज़ुबान बन गई, साबित करते हुए कि एक प्रादेशिक आवाज़ भी साम्राज्य की याद पर राज कर सकती है।

title_i18n.en: Prakrit Becomes the Language of Power

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Deccan Spoke Power in Prakrit
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब दक्खिन ने प्राकृत में बोली ताकत
